owner_reply.question: One real privacy issue remains in navigation: the current 15-second stage appears only on a tie, so its timing reveals the tie to everyone even if the label is hidden. I recommend a fixed 15-second route-setting window every round from Round 2, with only the Officer receiving tie-choice controls when needed. Should we preserve tie privacy this way, or allow players to infer ties from timing?
owner_reply.answer: Use the fixed 15-second window; keep ties private (Recommended)

supersedes: The tie-only navigation-stage timing in P10 and Designer request R10. P10 tie eligibility and authoritative random fallback, P09 sequential confirmations and P11 Round 1 movement remain unchanged.
confirmed_rules: From Round 2 onward, every round that reaches navigation has a fixed server-authoritative 15000-millisecond route-setting window before Captain and Officer confirmations. Round 1 retains its fixed Start-to-Junction movement and first-election sequence.

The full window applies to a tie, a non-tie, a retained Hack Spaceship override and an unavailable Officer. An early Officer choice cannot shorten the window; no client animation or reconnect may restart or extend it.

Only the currently eligible Officer receives tie-choice controls, and only for a genuine unresolved tie after applying any retained Hack Spaceship override. Other viewers receive no tie flag or tie-specific phase identity, wording, sound or animation.

Keep ties private through both projected data and timing. Public route-setting phase identity, interval and updates must not distinguish tie versus non-tie or expose whether or when the Officer selected a direction.

If a genuine tie remains without an accepted eligible Officer response at the deadline, use the existing authoritative equal-probability Blue/Red fallback. An absent or unavailable Officer does not skip the fixed window.

After the full route-setting interval, retain Captain-first then Officer confirmation under P09, with existing unavailable-office and timeout handling. Confirmation is not a veto, and navigation still makes exactly one movement per round.

Only the existing authorized office views receive final direction. Do not disclose totals, separate Captain weight, pre-override direction or detailed public route progress. P27 Blackhole presentation and the full Jail vote remain unchanged.
implementation_recommendations: Integration should define a neutral phase such as NAV_SETTING in the next exact contract tuple. This wire name is a technical recommendation, not a separately approved game rule.

Backend should persist the common interval and private Officer selection atomically, retain idempotent receipt/deadline handling, and avoid public revision/event differences caused only by a private tie choice.

Frontend and Designer should show the same neutral course-setting treatment and countdown for every outcome; derive the Officer controls from authorized offers. Reconnect resumes the existing server interval.

Verify paired tie/non-tie public projections and timing, early/late Officer choice, absent Officer, retained ship hack, zero-zero tie, duplicate/stale deadline delivery, reconnect and unchanged Round 1/historical-tuple behavior.

version_boundary.required_change: Allocate a new immutable engine/ruleset/source-hash tuple before runtime adoption. Do not rewrite the current authority manifest or its hash-bound specification files; existing matches retain their pinned behavior.
